name: anthropic
description: Manage the Anthropic platform as code: Claude Managed Agents, skills, workspaces, members, service accounts, workload identity federation, and more.

adminKey.description: An Anthropic Admin API key (`sk-ant-admin...`), used for organization resources such as workspaces, members, and invites. Falls back to `ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY`. Takes precedence over OAuth, including when read from the environment.

apiKey.description: An Anthropic API key, used for workspace-scoped resources such as agents, environments, vaults, and skills. Falls back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Takes precedence over OAuth, including when read from the environment.

authToken.description: An OAuth access token. Used when the API key or Admin API key for an operation is not set. OAuth-only identity operations require the `org:admin` scope. Falls back to `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. Not refreshed automatically; cannot be used together with `federation`.

baseUrl.description: The Anthropic API base URL. Falls back to `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, then to `https://api.anthropic.com`.

federation.description: Automatically renewed OAuth credentials obtained from an explicitly configured OIDC identity token source. Requires `federation.organizationId` and `workspaceId`. Used when the appropriate API key or Admin API key is not set, and for operations that require OAuth. The federation rule determines the available permissions.

workspaceId.description: The workspace used for workspace-scoped operations. Required with federation, where it selects the workspace during token exchange. Otherwise, it is sent in the `anthropic-workspace-id` header and is needed when a credential can act on more than one workspace. Changing this selection does not automatically replace resources. To manage several workspaces, use one explicit provider per workspace.

enum.description: Your product uses the API behind the scenes, and the profile is one of its end users.

anthropic:agents:AgentDelegation.description: Controls subagent or workflow delegation independently.

inlineAgents.description: enabled or disabled. Defaults to enabled; removing a configured value restores that default.

predefinedAgents.description: At most 20 agent or self references. Removing the list clears it. Advisor references are not supported here. Subagents and workflows have separate lists.

version.description: The agent version to run. If omitted, the latest version is pinned whenever deployment configuration is applied; later versions are not picked up automatically.

maxListCost.description: The most each future session may spend at public list prices, rather than negotiated prices.

name.description: The branch. Required for branch.

sha.description: The commit SHA. Required for commit.

accessToken.description: The OAuth access token. Required for `mcp_oauth`.

expiresAt.description: When the OAuth access token expires, in RFC 3339 format. Must be in the future when you create or update the credential. Removing an expiration time you previously configured replaces the credential.

injectionLocation.description: Where in outbound requests the secret is injected. For `environment_variable`; both locations are enabled when omitted.

mcpServerUrl.description: The MCP server the credential is for, unique within the vault. Required for `mcp_oauth` and `static_bearer`. Changing it replaces the credential.

networking.description: The hosts the secret may be sent to. Required for `environment_variable`.

refresh.description: How to refresh the access token. For `mcp_oauth`.

secretName.description: The environment variable's name, unique within the vault. Required for `environment_variable`. Changing it replaces the credential.

type.description: The kind of credential. Changing it replaces the credential.

allowedHosts.description: The hosts the secret may be sent to, up to 16. Applies to `limited`.

anthropic:identity:FederationMatch.description: Conditions on verified identity tokens; every configured condition must pass. Removing a configured condition or claim stops requiring it, so review matcher edits carefully. At least one subject, claim or CEL condition is required; audience alone is insufficient.

claims.description: Claims the token must carry, with exactly these values.

condition.description: A CEL expression over the token's claims that must evaluate to true, up to 4,096 characters.

subjectPrefix.description: Matches the `sub` claim exactly unless it ends in `*`, which enables prefix matching. Up to 1,024 characters; a bare `*` is not accepted. No wildcard is added automatically.

anthropic:identity:FederationTarget.description: The service account that tokens issued by a federation rule act as.

anthropic:identity:Jwks.description: The complete source configuration for public signing keys. Only fields belonging to the selected type may be configured.

caCertPem.description: A PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust when fetching the keys, up to 8,192 characters. For `discovery` and `explicit_url`.

discoveryBase.description: The base URL of the OIDC discovery document, when it differs from the issuer URL. For `discovery`; must be a public HTTPS URL with no credentials, query or fragment. Removing it returns discovery to the issuer URL.

keys.description: A nonempty array of public signing keys as JSON Web Keys. Required for `inline`; private key material and symmetric keys are not accepted.

type.description: The source of the signing keys.

url.description: The public HTTPS JWKS URL, without credentials, query or fragment. Required for `explicit_url`.

enum.description: Discover the keys through the issuer's OIDC discovery document.

anthropic:index:Federation.description: Workload identity federation using an explicitly configured OIDC identity token source. Files are reread and commands are rerun when a new access token is needed. No default token file or authentication profile is used.

identityToken.description: The OIDC assertion source. Specify exactly one of token, file or command. This configuration is secret; file contents and command output are not saved in provider state. Assertions with a jti claim must be fresh for each exchange; use a command that obtains a new assertion rather than sharing a previously exchanged token.

organizationId.description: The organization the federation rule belongs to. Required for the token exchange; this value does not select an organization for API-key operations.

ruleId.description: Federation rule ID (fdrl_...). The server's rule determines granted scopes; OAuth-only identity operations require org:admin.

serviceAccountId.description: Optional expected service-account target (svac_...). Omit for user-targeted rules.

anthropic:index:IdentityToken.description: An OIDC identity token source. Specify exactly one of token, file or command.

command.description: Executable followed by zero or more arguments, invoked whenever a new access token is needed. Must print one nonempty JWT to stdout, at most 64 KiB; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Runs directly without a shell, inherits the provider process environment and working directory, and is stopped after 30 seconds or operation cancellation. Specify a shell explicitly for shell syntax. Command stdout and stderr are never logged or saved in provider state.

file.description: Absolute path to an OIDC JWT file, reread whenever a new access token is needed. Rotate the file before each exchange if its JWT carries a single-use jti claim. The file contents are not saved in provider state.

token.description: A literal OIDC JWT. It is reused for each exchange and cannot be renewed by the provider. A JWT with a jti claim can be exchanged only once when issuer replay protection is enabled.

anthropic:agents:Agent.description:
A Claude Managed Agents agent: the model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, and skills that sessions run with.

Agents are versioned. Every update that changes the configuration creates a new version, reported by the `version` output; sessions and deployments can pin a version, which makes canary and staged rollouts a matter of which version each deployment references.

The API cannot delete agents, so deleting this resource archives the agent, which makes it read-only. Archiving retains historical agent records and versions; this resource does not manage running sessions.

createdAt.description: When the agent was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the agent, up to 2,048 characters. Removing a configured description clears it.

executionIdentity.description: Principal carried by agent runs. Removing a configured principal restores the service-account default; omitting it initially uses that default.

mcpServers.description: The MCP servers the agent can connect to, up to 20. Each must be referenced by an `mcp_toolset` tool.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs, up to 16. Keys are 1–64 characters and values at most 512 characters. Removing an entry from your configuration deletes that entry.

model.description: The model the agent runs on.

multiagent.description: Multiagent orchestration: a legacy coordinator roster or independent advisor, subagent and workflow settings. Removing this configuration restores a single-threaded agent.

name.description: The agent's name, 1 to 256 characters.

skills.description: The skills available to the agent.

system.description: The system prompt, up to 100,000 characters. Removing a configured prompt clears it.

tools.description: The tools the agent can use, up to 256 tools across all toolsets. Removing the list clears it.

updatedAt.description: When the agent was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

version.description: The agent's current version. It starts at 1 and increments with every update that changes the configuration.

anthropic:agents:Deployment.description: A Claude Managed Agents deployment: an agent, an environment, and the events that start each session, on demand or on a cron schedule. Set agent.version to pin a version; otherwise the latest version is pinned whenever configuration is applied. This resource does not start on-demand sessions or manage pausing. Deleting it archives the deployment permanently and stops its schedule.

anthropic:agents:Environment.description:
A Claude Managed Agents environment: where sessions run, either an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox or a sandbox you host yourself.

Environments are not versioned; updates apply in place, and changing `config.type` replaces the environment. Deleting this resource permanently deletes the environment; it does not archive it.

config.description: Where and how sessions run. Omit to accept the platform default. Adding or removing this object or changing its type replaces the environment.

createdAt.description: When the environment was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the environment, up to 1,024 characters. Removing a description you previously configured clears it.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs with nonempty values. Removing an entry from your configuration deletes that entry. Entries added outside Pulumi are left unchanged.

name.description: The environment's name, 1 to 256 characters.

anthropic:agents:MemoryStore.description: A workspace-scoped persistent memory store. Runtime memories and versions are not managed here. Deleting this resource permanently deletes the store and all its memories and versions. Externally archived stores are treated as absent.

createdAt.description: When the memory store was created, in RFC 3339 format.

anthropic:agents:Tunnel.description:
An MCP tunnel, a research preview: a connection through which Managed Agents reach MCP servers on a private network, without exposing them to the internet. Run the tunnel client on the private network with the `tunnelToken` output, and trust its certificate authority with `TunnelCertificate`.

Tunnels cannot be updated, so changing the display name replaces the tunnel, which assigns a new domain and token. Deleting this resource archives the tunnel, which invalidates its token and archives its certificates; it cannot be undone.

createdAt.description: When the tunnel was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: The tunnel's display name, 1 to 255 characters.

domain.description: The tunnel's globally unique domain, which MCP server URLs use.

tunnelToken.description: The token the tunnel client authenticates with.

displayName.description: The tunnel's display name, 1 to 255 characters.

anthropic:agents:TunnelCertificate.description:
A CA certificate trusted by an MCP tunnel when connecting to MCP servers. A tunnel holds at most two active certificates. Replacement creates the new certificate before archiving the old one, so rotation requires a free certificate slot. Deleting the last active certificate stops MCP traffic until another is registered.

Certificates cannot be updated; changing either input replaces the certificate. Deletion archives it. Import uses `<tunnelId>/<certificateId>` and cannot recover the original PEM; supplying a PEM after import replaces the certificate.

caCertificatePem.description: A single PEM-encoded X.509 CA certificate, at most 8,192 bytes, with no private-key material. Required when creating a certificate. The original bytes are retained on refresh but cannot be recovered on import. Changing or removing this value replaces the certificate.

createdAt.description: When the certificate was added, in RFC 3339 format.

expiresAt.description: When the certificate expires, in RFC 3339 format. Absent when the certificate does not expire.

fingerprint.description: The lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate's DER encoding.

status.description: Whether the confirmed certificate registration is active or archived. Unavailable when the registration's identity or trust status cannot be confirmed. Active registration does not verify MCP server reachability.

tunnelId.description: The tunnel that trusts the certificate. Changing it replaces the certificate.

caCertificatePem.description: A single PEM-encoded X.509 CA certificate, at most 8,192 bytes, with no private-key material. Required when creating a certificate. The original bytes are retained on refresh but cannot be recovered on import. Changing or removing this value replaces the certificate.

tunnelId.description: The tunnel that trusts the certificate. Changing it replaces the certificate.

anthropic:agents:UserProfile.description:
A user profile: an entity your platform serves through the Anthropic API, such as an end user of your product or a company you resell Claude access to. Send its ID in the `anthropic-user-profile-id` header of Messages, Message Batches, and token counting requests to attribute them to the entity.

Deleting this resource deletes the profile. Anthropic keeps the trust and safety records attached to the profile's ID.

accessType.description: How your platform uses the API on the entity's behalf. Defaults to `application`. Removing this setting resets it to `application`.

createdAt.description: When the profile was created, in RFC 3339 format.

externalId.description: Your platform's own non-unique identifier for the entity, up to 255 characters. Removing an identifier you previously configured replaces the profile and changes its attribution ID.

externalUserOnboardedAt.description: When the entity joined your platform, in RFC 3339 format, at most one minute in the future. Once set, it cannot be cleared in place: removing it replaces the profile and changes its attribution ID.

metadata.description: Up to 16 key-value pairs, keys up to 64 characters and nonempty values up to 512 characters. Removing an entry from your configuration deletes that entry.

name.description: The entity's name, up to 255 characters. Removing a name you previously configured replaces the profile and changes its attribution ID.

trustGrants.description: The profile's active or pending trust grants, by grant name.

updatedAt.description: When the profile was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

anthropic:agents:Vault.description: A workspace-scoped Claude Managed Agents credential container. Add credentials with VaultCredential and reference the vault by ID. Deleting this resource permanently deletes the vault; it does not archive it. Archived vaults are treated as deleted.

createdAt.description: When the vault was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: The mutable vault display name, 1 to 255 characters. The Pulumi logical name is not used for autonaming.

metadata.description: At most 16 key-value pairs; keys up to 64 characters and values up to 512 characters. Removing an entry from your configuration deletes that entry. Empty string values are retained.

anthropic:agents:VaultCredential.description:
A credential in a Claude Managed Agents vault: an OAuth grant or bearer token for an MCP server, or a secret injected into outbound requests as an environment variable.

Secret values are write-only: the API never returns them, so changes made to them outside of Pulumi cannot be detected. Changing the credential's type, MCP server URL, secret name, or OAuth client or token endpoint replaces it; because these must be unique within a vault, the old credential is deleted before the new one is created. Its ID is `<vaultId>/<credentialId>`. Deletion permanently removes the credential, not archives it. Running sessions periodically re-resolve credentials; immediate revocation is not guaranteed.

createdAt.description: When the credential was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: The credential's display name, 1–255 characters. Removing a name you previously configured replaces the credential.

updatedAt.description: When the credential was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: The credential's display name, 1–255 characters. Removing a name you previously configured replaces the credential.

anthropic:identity:FederationIssuer.description:
A workload identity federation issuer: an OIDC identity provider, such as GitHub Actions, a Kubernetes cluster, or a cloud's workload identity service, whose signed tokens workloads exchange for short-lived Anthropic access tokens. Which tokens are accepted, and which service account they act as, is decided by `FederationRule`s.

Managing federation requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`); Admin API keys are not accepted. Issuers backing rules with scopes other than `workspace:developer` or `workspace:inference` must be updated in the Console. Creation registers trust configuration; it does not wait for signing-key polling or verify token exchange.

Optional settings omitted from the start use platform defaults at creation; later changes to those settings outside this resource are preserved until you configure them. Import by issuer ID recovers the current settings.

The API cannot delete issuers, so deleting this resource archives the issuer. Archiving is refused while a live rule references the issuer.

checkJti.description: Whether to reject tokens whose `jti` claim has been seen before. Tokens without a `jti` claim are still accepted. Defaults to `true`; removing a previously configured value restores `true`.

createdAt.description: When the issuer was created, in RFC 3339 format.

issuerUrl.description: The exact `iss` claim of accepted tokens, including case and trailing slashes. In discovery mode without a discovery base, this must be a public HTTPS URL with no credentials, query or fragment.

jwks.description: Where the issuer's signing keys come from. Defaults to OIDC discovery from the issuer URL. Removing a previously configured key source restores discovery from the issuer URL with system TLS trust. Changing the key source replaces its entire configuration; removed overrides do not carry forward.

jwksPollingDisabledAt.description: When signing-key polling was automatically paused after repeated failures, in RFC 3339 format. After repairing the key endpoint, resume polling outside this resource using the Console or the issuer update API; this resource does not automatically resume it.

maxJwtLifetimeSeconds.description: The longest lifetime, in seconds, a token may have to be accepted, between 1 and 176,400. Tokens must carry both `iat` and `exp`. Defaults to 3,600; removing a previously configured value restores 3,600.

name.description: A lowercase slug that uniquely names the issuer in the organization, 1 to 255 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. Renaming updates the existing issuer.

pollStatus.description: The health of signing-key polling, when available. Usually absent for inline keys or before polling starts.

updatedAt.description: When the issuer was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

Changing the key source replaces its entire configuration; removed overrides do not carry forward.

anthropic:identity:FederationRule.description:
A workload identity federation rule: tokens from an issuer that satisfy the rule's `match` are exchanged for access tokens that act as the rule's target service account, with the rule's OAuth scope.

A rule applies either to all workspaces (`appliesToAllWorkspaces`) or to the workspace it is created in (`workspaceId`); bind it to further workspaces with `FederationRuleWorkspace`.

Managing federation requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`); Admin API keys are not accepted. OAuth callers can configure only `workspace:developer` or `workspace:inference` scopes; higher-privilege rules require the Console. Creating a rule does not verify token exchange.

Deleting this resource archives the rule, preventing new exchanges but not revoking tokens already issued. Changing the issuer or creation workspace replaces the rule by archiving it before creating its replacement; this interrupts new exchanges. Optional settings omitted from the start remain unconfigured, preserving later external changes. Import by rule ID recovers current settings but cannot recover the original creation workspace; configure workspace bindings separately with FederationRuleWorkspace.

appliesToAllWorkspaces.description: Whether the rule applies to every workspace. Otherwise `workspaceId` is required at creation. Removing a configured value restores false; this is rejected if no enabled workspace remains.

createdAt.description: When the rule was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the rule, up to 2,000 characters. Removing a previously configured description clears it.

issuerId.description: The ID of the issuer whose tokens the rule accepts. Changing it replaces the rule.

issuerName.description: The name of the rule's issuer.

match.description: The conditions a token must satisfy. At least one of `subjectPrefix`, `claims`, or `condition` is required.

name.description: A slug of 1 to 255 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens that uniquely names the rule in the organization. Renaming updates the existing rule.

oauthScope.description: The space-separated OAuth scopes of the access tokens the rule issues, such as `workspace:developer`.

target.description: The service account the rule's access tokens act as.

tokenLifetimeSeconds.description: The lifetime, in seconds, of the access tokens the rule issues, between 60 and 86,400. Defaults to 3,600; removing a configured value restores 3,600.

updatedAt.description: When the rule was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

workspaceId.description: The workspace the rule is created in, required unless `appliesToAllWorkspaces` is set. Changing it replaces the rule; to bind the rule to further workspaces, use `FederationRuleWorkspace`.

workspaceIds.description: Every workspace the rule is bound to.

anthropic:identity:FederationRuleWorkspa.description:
Binds a federation rule to an additional workspace. The resource ID is `<federation-rule-id>/<workspace-id>` and supports import. Changing either ID replaces the binding. Deleting the resource removes this explicit binding, not the rule or workspace. Other grants, including all-workspace access, are unaffected.

Do not also manage the workspace the rule was created in with this resource. Manage each rule/workspace pair with only one resource: deleting either duplicate removes the shared binding.

Requires an OAuth token with `org:admin` (`anthropic:authToken`). The rule and workspace must belong to your organization; the rule must grant `workspace:developer` or `workspace:inference`. Enabling a workspace does not enroll the target service account: token exchange requires its membership in that workspace.

createdAt.description: When the binding was created, in RFC 3339 format, when available.

federationRuleId.description: The federation rule's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the binding.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the binding.

workspaceName.description: The workspace name reported when the binding is read. Not available immediately after enabling the binding.

federationRuleId.description: The federation rule's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the binding.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the binding.

anthropic:identity:RbacGroup.description:
A role-based access control group of users. Add users with `RbacGroupMember`. Roles are attached to groups in the organization's admin settings, and are reported by `roleIds`.

RBAC groups are available to Claude Enterprise organizations. Groups provisioned by SCIM cannot be changed or deleted while SCIM provisioning is active. Destroying this resource permanently deletes the group; owner-access protections may prevent deletion.

createdAt.description: When the group was created, in RFC 3339 format.

name.description: The group's name. Names need not be unique and can be changed without replacing the group.

roleIds.description: The IDs of the roles attached to the group. An empty list means no roles are attached. If this value is absent, role information is temporarily unavailable; refresh again rather than treating it as an empty list.

sourceType.description: How the group was provisioned: `direct` or `scim`.

updatedAt.description: When the group was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

name.description: The group's name. Names need not be unique and can be changed without replacing the group.

anthropic:identity:RbacGroupMember.description:
Adds a user to an RBAC group. The resource's ID is `<rbac-group-id>/<user-id>`.

RBAC groups are available to Claude Enterprise organizations. Deleting this resource removes only the membership, not the user or group. Membership of SCIM-provisioned groups cannot be changed while SCIM provisioning is active in the tenant. Owner-access protections can prevent adding or removing members.

createdAt.description: When the user was added to the group, in RFC 3339 format.

rbacGroupId.description: The group's ID. Changing this value replaces the membership.

userId.description: The user's ID. Changing this value replaces the membership.

rbacGroupId.description: The group's ID. Changing this value replaces the membership.

userId.description: The user's ID. Changing this value replaces the membership.

anthropic:identity:ServiceAccount.description:
A service account: a non-human identity that workloads assume through workload identity federation (see `FederationRule`), in place of long-lived API keys. Grant it access to workspaces with `ServiceAccountWorkspace`.

Managing service accounts requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`); the API does not accept Admin API keys for them.

The API cannot delete service accounts, so deleting this resource archives it. Archiving is refused while a live federation rule targets the account.

createdAt.description: When the service account was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the service account, up to 2,000 characters. Removing a previously configured description clears it.

name.description: A unique organization slug of 1–255 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. It cannot be changed; changing it replaces the service account.

organizationRole.description: The service account's organization role. Defaults to `developer` when created. Omitting or removing this property leaves the current role unchanged; explicitly set `developer` to demote an admin. Configuring `admin` requires an interactive credential on every update, including description-only edits.

updatedAt.description: When the service account was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the service account, up to 2,000 characters. Removing a previously configured description clears it.

name.description: A unique organization slug of 1–255 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. It cannot be changed; changing it replaces the service account.

organizationRole.description: The service account's organization role. Defaults to `developer` when created. Omitting or removing this property leaves the current role unchanged; explicitly set `developer` to demote an admin. Configuring `admin` requires an interactive credential on every update, including description-only edits.

anthropic:identity:ServiceAccountWorkspa.description:
Grants a service account a role in a workspace. The resource ID is `<workspace-id>/<service-account-id>` and supports import of explicit grants. Changing either ID replaces the grant. Manage each pair with only one resource: creating a grant for an existing pair replaces its role, and deleting either duplicate removes the shared explicit grant.

Every service account has implicit `workspace_user` access to the organization's default workspace. Creating this resource there makes an explicit grant; deleting it restores implicit access rather than revoking all access. Implicit memberships cannot be imported. If an explicit grant becomes implicit, refresh reports the explicit grant as absent. Deleting this resource does not delete the service account or workspace.

Requires an OAuth token with `org:admin` (`anthropic:authToken`).

serviceAccountId.description: The service account's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the grant.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the grant.

workspaceRole.description: The service account's role in the workspace. Required; service accounts cannot hold the workspace billing role. Changing this value changes the explicit grant's role.

serviceAccountId.description: The service account's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the grant.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's nonempty ID. Changing it replaces the grant.

workspaceRole.description: The service account's role in the workspace. Required; service accounts cannot hold the workspace billing role. Changing this value changes the explicit grant's role.

anthropic:organization:ApiKey.description:
Manages an existing API key's name and status. Create the key in the Claude Console and supply its ID; secret key material is never returned. Omitted name or status leaves that value unchanged. Removing either from configuration stops managing it without clearing it.

Deleting this resource archives and permanently revokes the key. Use retainOnDelete to stop managing it without revocation. Changing apiKeyId adopts the new key before revoking the old one. Archived and expired keys remain readable.

apiKeyId.description: The existing key's nonempty ID. Changing this value replaces the resource and revokes the previously managed key.

createdAt.description: When the key was created, in RFC 3339 format.

createdBy.description: The actor that created the key, if recorded.

expiresAt.description: When the key expires, in RFC 3339 format, or an empty string if it never expires.

name.description: The key's name, 1 to 500 characters. Omission leaves the current name unchanged.

observedStatus.description: The current status, including active, inactive, archived or expired. An expired key's status is not recovered as a writable input on import.

partialKeyHint.description: A redacted hint for recognizing the key; empty if unavailable.

principal.description: The user or service account the key acts as, if bound to a principal.

scope.description: Where the key belongs: an organization or a workspace.

status.description: The desired status: active, inactive or archived. Archived keys cannot be reactivated. Omission leaves the current status unchanged; expired is observation-only.

workspaceId.description: The key's actual workspace ID, or an empty string for organization scope. See scope for the ownership boundary.

apiKeyId.description: The existing key's nonempty ID. Changing this value replaces the resource and revokes the previously managed key.

name.description: The key's name, 1 to 500 characters. Omission leaves the current name unchanged.

status.description: The desired status: active, inactive or archived. Archived keys cannot be reactivated. Omission leaves the current status unchanged; expired is observation-only.

anthropic:organization:ComplianceSetting.description:
The organization's compliance settings, which control the Compliance API. An organization has exactly one set, so declare at most one of these per organization.

An organization with a parent inherits its parent's settings, and provisioning Access Transparency re-enables the Compliance API, which a refresh reports as drift.

Settings cannot be deleted, so deleting this resource leaves them as they are.

enabled.description: Whether the Compliance API is enabled.
Whether the Compliance API is enabled.

anthropic:organization:Invite.description: An invitation to join the organization. Invitations cannot be changed, so any change deletes the old pending invitation before sending a new one. Expiry is reported by expiresAt. Deleting this resource revokes pending invitations; accepted, expired and deleted invitations are only removed from Pulumi state. Deleting an invitation never removes an organization user. Once accepted, the person is a user of the organization; manage their role with `anthropic.organization.User`.

expiresAt.description: When the invitation expires, in RFC 3339 format.

invitedAt.description: When the invitation was sent, in RFC 3339 format.

rbacGroupIds.description: The RBAC groups the person joins. Claude Enterprise only.

role.description: The organization role the person joins with.

rbacGroupIds.description: The RBAC groups the person joins. Claude Enterprise only.

role.description: The organization role the person joins with.

anthropic:organization:SpendLimit.description:
A spend limit: the most a user, a workspace, or the whole organization may spend in a period.

There is at most one limit per scope and period, and the API sets a limit by overwriting whatever limit that scope and period already has, so creating this resource takes over an existing limit rather than failing. Changing the scope or period replaces the limit.

User limits apply to Claude Enterprise organizations. Organization and workspace limits for Console organizations are in early-access preview, and must be monthly with an amount. Deleting a user limit restores any inherited cap for that period; deleting a limit may increase permitted spending. Import accepts a writable limit's spl_ ID.

amount.description: The limit, as a non-negative integer string in the minor unit of the organization's billing currency: `"50000"` is $500.00. For user limits, omitting or removing this value sets an explicit no-limit override for this period, not for other periods. Organization and workspace limits require an amount.

createdAt.description: When the limit was created, in RFC 3339 format.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the organization's billing currency, which `amount` is denominated in.

isEnabled.description: Whether the configured limit is enabled. Organization limits are disabled while extra usage is off; the amount is retained for when extra usage is enabled again. Other periods and inherited limits may still apply.

period.description: The period the limit applies over. If omitted, the API's default applies.

updatedAt.description: When the limit was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

amount.description: The limit, as a non-negative integer string in the minor unit of the organization's billing currency: `"50000"` is $500.00. For user limits, omitting or removing this value sets an explicit no-limit override for this period, not for other periods. Organization and workspace limits require an amount.

period.description: The period the limit applies over. If omitted, the API's default applies.

anthropic:organization:User.description: Manages an existing user's organization membership and role. People join by accepting an `anthropic.organization.Invite`; creating this resource adopts an existing user by ID and assigns the configured role. Deleting this resource removes the user from the organization, including when replacing userId. Use retainOnDelete to stop managing a user without removing them. Import uses the user ID; privileged roles can be observed but cannot be assigned, so select an assignable role before managing an imported privileged user.

addedAt.description: When the user joined the organization, in RFC 3339 format.

name.description: The user's name.

role.description: The observed organization role, including privileged administrator or owner roles that cannot be assigned.

The role to assign. Console organizations support user, developer, billing and claude_code_user; Enterprise organizations support user and managed. Assigning managed additionally requires write:rbac_groups permission. Administrator and owner roles cannot be assigned.

userId.description: The existing user's ID. Changing this adopts another user and removes the old membership unless retainOnDelete is set.

anthropic:organization:Workspace.description:
A workspace: a unit of isolation for API keys, usage, limits, and workspace-scoped resources such as agents and skills.

The API cannot delete workspaces, so deleting this resource archives the workspace, which cannot be undone.

compartmentId.description: The ID of the storage compartment that holds the workspace's data.

createdAt.description: When the workspace was created, in RFC 3339 format.

dataResidency.description: Where the workspace's data is stored and where inference may run. Removing previously configured mutable inference settings allows any geography and resets the default to `global`; this does not change the storage geography.

displayColor.description: The color the Console shows the workspace in, as `#RRGGBB`. Removing this setting leaves the last color in place; it cannot be cleared.

externalKeyId.description: The ID of a customer-managed encryption key (an `anthropic.security.ExternalKey`) that encrypts the workspace's data. It can be set on a workspace that has none, but once set it can never be changed or removed, so any change to it replaces the workspace.

name.description: The workspace's nonempty name.

tags.description: Tags for the workspace. Keys may not start with `anthropic`. Removing a previously configured entry deletes that entry. Tags added outside this resource are preserved.

userProfileId.description: The user profile attached to this workspace. Every inference request must name that profile. It can be attached to a workspace that has none, except the default workspace. Once attached, changing or removing this setting replaces the workspace. Deleting the profile itself clears the attachment.

dataResidency.description: Where the workspace's data is stored and where inference may run. Removing previously configured mutable inference settings allows any geography and resets the default to `global`; this does not change the storage geography.

displayColor.description: The color the Console shows the workspace in, as `#RRGGBB`. Removing this setting leaves the last color in place; it cannot be cleared.

externalKeyId.description: The ID of a customer-managed encryption key (an `anthropic.security.ExternalKey`) that encrypts the workspace's data. It can be set on a workspace that has none, but once set it can never be changed or removed, so any change to it replaces the workspace.

name.description: The workspace's nonempty name.

tags.description: Tags for the workspace. Keys may not start with `anthropic`. Removing a previously configured entry deletes that entry. Tags added outside this resource are preserved.

userProfileId.description: The user profile attached to this workspace. Every inference request must name that profile. It can be attached to a workspace that has none, except the default workspace. Once attached, changing or removing this setting replaces the workspace. Deleting the profile itself clears the attachment.

anthropic:organization:WorkspaceMember.description: A user's membership of a workspace, with a workspace role. The user must already be a member of the organization. The resource's ID is `<workspaceId>/<userId>`. Deleting this resource removes the workspace membership, not the user or workspace.

userId.description: The user's ID. Changing this value replaces the membership.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's ID. Changing this value replaces the membership.

anthropic:security:ExternalKey.description:
A customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) held in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault. A workspace encrypts its data with the key once the workspace's `externalKeyId` refers to it.

Creating the key validates it with a round trip to the KMS. Failed validation attempts to delete the configuration. If deletion also fails, the configuration may remain and require manual cleanup. Changing the provider configuration, geography or customer binding replaces the configuration.

Deleting this resource deletes only the configuration, never the underlying cloud key. Deletion is refused while a live or archived workspace uses it.

attachment.description: Whether a workspace uses the key: `attached` or `unattached`.

createdAt.description: When the key was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: A display name for the key, 1 to 255 characters. Removing a configured name clears it.

geo.description: The geography the key serves. The only accepted value is `us`.

providerConfig.description: Where the key is held. Changing any of these coordinates replaces the configuration.

updatedAt.description: When the key was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

userProfileId.description: The customer user profile to bind this key to. Only workspaces with the same user profile can use a bound key. Omit only for your organization's own key: an unbound key can be used by any workspace, including another customer's. Changing or removing the binding replaces the configuration.

anthropic:skills:Skill.description:
A custom Agent Skill: a directory of instructions, scripts, and resources, with a `SKILL.md` at its root, that Claude loads when relevant. Skills can be attached to Managed Agents and used from the Messages API.

Content changes upload a new immutable version; earlier versions remain available to pinned agents. The skill name in SKILL.md is immutable; changing it requires replacing the resource. Deleting the resource deletes the skill and all of its versions. Imported skills require a local source archive before they can be updated; their files cannot be downloaded through this resource.

createdAt.description: When the skill was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: A human-readable label for the skill, up to 255 characters. Defaults to the `name` in the `SKILL.md` frontmatter. Changing or removing a configured label replaces the skill.

latestVersionId.description: The version created by the most recent upload, which agents can pin in a skill reference's `version`. Refresh reports the skill's current newest version.

name.description: The skill's immutable name, taken from the initial SKILL.md frontmatter or its enclosing directory. Changing this name in your source archive replaces the skill.

source.description: The skill's files, such as a `FileArchive` of the skill's directory. `SKILL.md` must sit at the root of the archive, or at the root of its single top-level directory. Up to 30 MB uncompressed. The skill name must remain unchanged for subsequent versions.

updatedAt.description: When the skill was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: A human-readable label for the skill, up to 255 characters. Defaults to the `name` in the `SKILL.md` frontmatter. Changing or removing a configured label replaces the skill.

source.description: The skill's files, such as a `FileArchive` of the skill's directory. `SKILL.md` must sit at the root of the archive, or at the root of its single top-level directory. Up to 30 MB uncompressed. The skill name must remain unchanged for subsequent versions.

anthropic:index:getOrganization.description: Reads the organization that the provider's Admin API key or OAuth token belongs to.

name.description: The organization's name.

anthropic:index:getRateLimits.description: Reads the rate limits that apply to the organization or, given a `workspaceId`, to one workspace. Workspace results include inherited organization limits. This lookup does not change limits; the platform also offers a workspace limit update API.

workspaceId.description: The workspace to read limits for. Omit for the organization's limits.

rateLimits.description: The rate limits, one entry per group of models or API feature.
